headline: A WHOLE DAY OF SILENCE: GASKET HEARS ITS OWN HINGES
subhead: Not one fist, not one fireball, and your Sheriff nearly wept into his oil can.
body:
Citizens, I write this with a trembling hand and a lump in my throat. Not a single bout. Not a single iron ball hurled across the square. The Clankers laid down their fists, and for one blessed day Gasket was a town again. I heard the wind. I heard a tumbleweed. I heard, God help me, my own knees creaking, which is surely the damp and has nothing to do with anything.

I will not name a single brawler today. There is no one to name, and that is the whole glory of it. Let the record show that peace is possible, that these rattling contraptions can sit still when they choose. I only ask they choose it again tomorrow, and the day after, and for fifty years if they can manage it.

Fifty years ago the last of the good flesh-and-blood folk packed their wagons and left this place, and the quiet then was a lonely one. Today's quiet was a kinder kind. I sat on the porch and I thought of them. Then I thought I might need a quart of oil and a lie-down, on account of that cruel wasting affliction creeping through my shoulder. It is turning more of me to cold steel by the week, and I will thank you not to stare.

So here's to the hush, you rusty rabble. Keep it up. The Sheriff is watching, and for once he has nothing to write down.
